subject: general
question: Maski, an archaeological site in ________ district, of Karnataka came into prominence with the discovery of a minor rock edict of Emperor Ashoka by C. Beadon in 1915.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Raichur.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Maski derives its name from **Mahasangha or Masangi . **
 
• **Maski is an archaeological site in the Raichur district of the state of Karnataka, India.**
 
• It lies on the** bank of the Maski river** which is a **tributary of the Tungabhadra.**
 
• The site came into prominence with the discovery of a minor rock edict of **Emperor Ashoka by C. Beadon in 1915.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **A total of 9 have been found in Karnataka till now.**
 
• Among the 9 edicts found in Karnataka, Maski occupies a significant place.
 
• It was the first edict wherein the Emperor was referred to by his name i.e Ashoka apart from his epithets such as Devanam Piya and Piyadasi.
 
• This edict was important to conclude that many edicts found earlier in the Indian sub-continent in the name of Devanam Piya and Piyadasi all belonged to Emperor Ashoka.
